why: Quote is verbatim (desktop.md:719, whole line read; the second sentence only tightens the type rule to JSON boolean true, it does not reverse anything). The identifier half of the finding is also true: managed-policy.ts:501 is `export const MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS = [` and neither `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` nor `browserExternalPageTools` appears in it, and `grep -ran` for both names over the repo hits only docs/spec/JSON sweep files. What refutes the finding as filed is its CONSEQUENCE, which is the exact recurring shape this repo warns about (identifier unwired, consequence false because a layer above already handles it): (1) 'no managed off-switch' is wrong. A managed `permissionDsl` deny rule is the documented real boundary and it reaches `browser_tool`. managed-policy.ts:298-301 states it in so many words ('An admin who needs a real boundary uses a managed `permissionDsl` deny rule, which our deterministic gate applies BEFORE the judge is consulted at all'); mode-manager.ts:2103-2117 runs `deniedToolPatterns`/`disallowedTools` and 2129 runs `toolRules` deny BEFORE the ALWAYS_ALLOWED_TOOLS set that contains 'browser_tool' (mode-manager.ts:2001), and the comment at 2010-2013 names the deny check as 'the lever'; pi-agent.ts:1729-1760 applies `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny`, which removes a whole-tool-denied binding from the exposed tool set, and `browser_tool` is a static binding (harness-tool-descriptor.ts:160, :293). (2) A second off-switch exists one layer down: `getBrowserToolEnabled()` (config/storage.ts:1053) gates `mcp__session__browser_tool` out of the session tool defs at pi-agent.ts:1610-1612, defaulting from the bundled `apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json` (`browserToolEnabled`, storage.ts:91/179), so a corporate build can ship it off. correctedState: Neither managed key is read -- `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (managed-policy.ts:501) holds 32 keys and contains neither `browserExternalPageTools` nor `disableBrowserExternalNavigation`, and there is no URL allowlist, domain or origin check anywhere in `browser-tool-runtime.ts` / `browser-tools.ts` (grep -ranEi for allowlist|blocklist|domain|origin returns nothing). But 'no managed off-switch' is false: an admin CAN remove the agent's browser access through managed policy, via a `permissionDsl` deny rule on `browser_tool` -- deny is evaluated before the ALWAYS_ALLOWED_TOOLS membership at mode-manager.ts:2103/2129 vs :2001, and `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (pi-agent.ts:1729ff) strips the binding outright -- and a build can ship `browserToolEnabled: false` in `config-defaults.json`, which filters `mcp__session__browser_tool` at pi-agent.ts:1610. What we genuinely lack is finer-grained than the finding says: our levers are all-or-nothing and agent-only. There is no external-page-vs-localhost distinction (Claude's `browserExternalPageTools` keeps Claude's tools on localhost previews while removing them on external pages; our deny removes the tool everywhere), tool rules match on tool NAME only via glob (`matchesToolPermissionRule`, mode-manager.ts:238-257) so no URL-scoped rule is expressible, and nothing can block the USER's own navigation in the Electron Browser pane the way `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` does -- `browser-pane-manager.ts` and `browser-cdp.ts` carry no allowlist/domain logic at all.
